datasets.title: Geodata of Shelters at Hadalat Border Crossing, Jordan-Syria Border
datasets.description: This data illustrates shelters in the area of the Hadalat crossing on the Syrian-Jordanian border. Using a satellite image collected by the Deimos-2 satellite on 13 July 2016, UNOSAT located 2,132 probable shelters. This is a 9% increase in shelters since the previous UNOSAT analysis done using an image collected 14 May 2016. Due to the small size and the irregularity of the shelters it is likely that some shelters may have been missed in this analysis, or some shelters were included erroneously.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/geodata-of-shelters-at-hadalat-border-crossing-jordan-syria-border]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts manually reviewed Deimos-2 satellite imagery acquired on 13 July 2016 of the Hadalat border crossing area, comparing it with a prior image from 14 May 2016 to identify and map shelter structures. Probable shelters were digitized as point or polygon features with confidence ratings and validation flags, representing a 9% increase from the previous survey period.

sources.name: UN Operational Satellite Applications Programme (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Satellite-based shelter detection using Deimos-2 imagery from July 2016, identifying 2,132 probable shelter structures through manual image analysis and comparison with prior surveys
